---
title: "Short"
subtitle: "Two halves, with a facilitator"
---
This format fills a slot of two to three hours, with nothing to install, nothing sent to a class chart and nothing preregistered. The session works on a field experiment, in which emails that differed only in the name that signed them were sent to public housing authorities in the United States, and on a claim of the original authors (OAs) that five analysts reanalysed for the robustness study of SCORE (Multi100; Aczel et al. 2026). You meet the claim and the five analysts, write the estimand statement behind the claim, and reproduce one of the five reanalyses, whichever you choose. Then you try a few alternative analyses from the menu of the case study, read the place of the one that you would defend among the 64 specifications on the curve of the claim, and end on the replication that tested the claim with new data.

You leave with an estimand statement of your own and a reproduced value whose dependence on the defaults of the software you can explain. You also know where the analysis that you would defend sits among every justifiable analysis of these data, and you have met a claim that holds under every analysis of one sample and still failed on new data.

## How you work

The session runs on its deck, whose slides run R inside your browser, with the data already in place, so that you follow and work in one place. Open the deck in a tab of its own and keep this page open beside it. Each half of the session has a page that lists its steps in order, and every step that you work at the keyboard has a button that opens the deck at the slide of the task. The browser lab, a page of the course site that holds the same tasks outside the deck, is the fallback, and a second button opens it at the same task. The [exercise](exercise.qmd) page sets out the tasks of the session and the tool in which each is done. The slides are on the [slides page](slides.qmd), and each half opens with a link to its place in the deck.

[Open the deck](slides.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Open the browser lab](../../lab.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The class writes its estimand statements and its reproduced values in the chat and sends them at the same moment, so the session needs a facilitator.

## The parts of the session

- **[Before the session](before.qmd)** (about an hour). You read the background page and open the deck once on the machine that you will bring.
- **[The exercise](exercise.qmd).** The claim, the five analysts and the tasks of the session, which are all done in the deck.
- **[First half – The claim and its reproduction](half-1.qmd).** The half sets out the three Rs and the SCORE programme, the paper and the five analysts, the estimand statement and the causal graph, and it ends with your reproduction of one of the five reanalyses.
- **[Second half – Exploration and replication](half-2.qmd).** After a short break, you work through the specification menu, try a few analyses of your own, place one of them on the curve of 64, and meet the replication with new data.
- **[After the session](after.qmd)** (as long as you like). The page sets out the rest of the exercise and where to go next.
